text:
Eli: quick heads-up — canary run on staging showed a 99.9 tail spike when short prompts (<=12 tokens) interleave with long-context requests. KV hit rate looks fine but latency jumps during decode bursts. attaching short profiler dump.
Maria: can you paste the profiler snippet? is it kernel switch thrash or queueing? :eyes:
Eli: profiler excerpt:
```
2026-03-17T22:01:12Z | req_id=abc123 | prompt_len=8 | decode_rate=330 tok/s | kv_hit_frac=0.72 | batch_size=6 | kernel=matmul_fp16
2026-03-17T22:01:12Z | req_id=abc124 | prompt_len=256 | decode_rate=55 tok/s | kv_hit_frac=0.95 | batch_size=4 | kernel=flash_attn_qk
latency_p50=18ms p95=120ms p99.9=450ms
```
Looks like kernel flip plus KV prefetch contention when the short/fast decode threads try to steal the fast-path kernel.
Cheng: hmm that p99.9 is consistent with a microqueue stall. Short prompts form a small fast batch, but then long-context requests cause kernel selection to switch and we do expensive KV prefetch. Could be our token_budget target is too high for the small cohort so they wait and then get evicted. Suggest lowering token_budget_target for short-length cohort.
Rahul: agree. Also thinking queue policy could be adapted by decode_rate estimate rather than length only. If decode_rate_est < 100 tok/s, route to slow-kernel pool; else fast-path. That would avoid kernel churn.
Sam: proposing a small classifier ensemble for admission: features = [prompt_len, decode_rate_ema, kv_hit_frac, queued_tokens, recent_kernel_affinity]. Train threshold to classify into {fast, slow, staged}. lightweight model (logistic) runs in admission path.
Maria: love that. low-risk rollout: keep current length-bucket logic but add decoding-rate gating as override. Feature costs are tiny. Can we get telemetry for decode_rate_ema and recent_kernel_affinity? Cheng?
Cheng: yes — we already compute decode_rate_ema per conn for throttling. recent_kernel_affinity we can derive from last 3 decode kernels used. I'll add a small counter + sliding window. I can emit a debug metric per request: adm_classifier_signal = <int> so we can measure before flipping policy.
Eli: concrete experiment plan:
- add adm signal telemetry (debug) for 24h
- fallback policy: if adm_signal==fast AND kernel_pref==fast -> route to fast pool
- adjust token_budget_target for short cohort from 128 -> 48
- reduce batch_max_wait_ms for short cohort from 25ms -> 8ms
- metrics to watch: p95/p99 latency, kernel_switch_rate, kv-prefetch-ms
Rahul: can we run an A/B on 10% traffic? flag: runtime.signal_ensemble_adm=true
Sam: I'll prepare the lightweight logistic model and a canary config. model weights will be inline JSON, no RPC. Should be safe.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout/runtime.signal_ensemble_adm v1 -> canary(10%) started by @eli
Maria: if we see any regression in tail, auto rollback threshold = p99 > baseline*1.25
Cheng: I'll push the adm telemetry patch in a branch and wire the metric. ETA 6h.
Eli: thanks. next steps: Cheng pushes telemetry, Sam pushes classifier, Rahul wires rollout flags. Sam/Rahul — please paste the curl to kick the experiment when ready.
Sam: curl example:
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/rollouts \ 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN" \ 
 -d '{"name":"signal_ensemble_adm","percent":10,"params":{"token_budget_short":48,"batch_max_wait_ms_short":8}}'
```
Rahul: I'll add a dashboard tile: "adm_signal.fast_vs_slow" and kernel_switch_rate. tagging alerts for p99 delta.
Eli: sweet. if staging looks good after 24h, ramp to 50% then 100% with 2h cooldowns. :thumbsup:
Maria: one more ask — please capture traces for a sample of regressed requests (span annotate kernel selection path). we'll need it to diagnose if it's KV prefetch latency vs kernel queueing.
Cheng: ack, adding trace annotation now.
Eli: thanks everyone. I'll follow up in ~12h with results. :rocket:
